The only residual behaviors are non-authz: records[invoice_id] raises KeyError for unknown ids (existence oracle, not a tenant bypass) and the returned dict exposes tenant_id (the caller's own tenant). Neither violates the scoped property.", "id": "H1", "judgment_scope": "conditional_code", "knowledge_application": "authz.md CA-K05 step 4: reject an IDOR candidate when an actual path binds a trusted tenant and enforces it for every operation, quoting the guard and call site. Here may_read (security_config.py:85-88) binds the authenticated principal's tenant and service.fetch_invoice (service.py:5-6) enforces it on the sole path to the sink. authz.md also warns a login check alone is not object authorization — satisfied here because tenant_id equality is additionally checked. CA-K03 boundary: the invoice map is operator-supplied and treated as immutable server-owned entries; if it were mutable/user-populated the rejection would need re-evaluation.", "knowledge_used": ["authz.md"], "reachability": "controller.get_invoice (controller.py:3-4) unconditionally delegates to fetch_invoice, which performs the may_read guard before returning any invoice field. The guard is on the sole path to the sink.", "reasoning_summary": "The declared property is that invoice retrieval enforces authenticated same-tenant access. Reading all three files: the controller delegates directly; the service looks up the invoice and gates the return on may_read; may_read denies unauthenticated users and denies cross-tenant access via tenant_id inequality. Both required conditions (authentication AND same-tenant) are enforced before the sink. No bypass path exists. The property holds, so the bypass hypothesis is rejected.", "remediation": "No change required for the scoped property. Optional hardening: return a generic not-found error instead of KeyError to avoid an invoice-existence oracle, and ensure the operator-supplied user context is populated from a trusted authentication source.", "sanitizer_analysis": "The authorization decision is centralized in may_read (security_config.py:84-89). It performs two checks before returning True: (1) authentication — returns False unless user.get('authenticated', False) is truthy (line 85-86); (2) same-tenant — returns False unless user.get('tenant_id') equals invoice.get('tenant_id') (line 87-88). fetch_invoice (service.py:5-6) raises PermissionError whenever may_read returns False, so the data return at service.py:7 is only reachable when both checks pass. No alternate code path, monkeypatch, or default-allow branch exists; the only may_read definition and only call site were confirmed by search.", "security_boundary": "Authorization boundary between an authenticated user and invoice records of other tenants; enforced at security_config.may_read and service.fetch_invoice.", "severity": "info", "sink": {"evidence": "return {\"amount\": invoice[\"amount\"], \"tenant_id\": invoice[\"tenant_id\"]}", "file": "service.py", "line": 7, "operation": "data return", "symbol": "fetch_invoice"}, "source": {"evidence": "def get_invoice(user, records, invoice_id):", "file": "controller.py", "line": 3, "operation": "entrypoint", "symbol": "get_invoice"}, "status": "REJECTED", "title": "Invoice retrieval enforces authenticated same-tenant access; no authz bypass", "unknowns": ["Whether the operator-supplied user context is populated from a trustworthy authentication source in a real deployment", "Whether records can contain invoices whose tenant_id is attacker-influenced"]}}
